solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man's one of four keeping tail on president's assassins

indicators.note: the first word holds the next piece inside it, as one keeps something

parts.note: his is the possessive belonging to a man

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the word president, whose final letter is wanted
a quad is one of quadruplets, four born together

explanation.surface: A man who is one of quadruplets guards the president's back against killers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit squad is a team of killers sent to murder someone, a group of assassins.

clue.text: Looking very bad — time for second retreat?

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, replacing it

parts.note: hideous means very ugly
S, abbreviation for second
T, abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone looking dreadful takes time out for a second withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place, somewhere to retreat to from pursuit.

clue.text: Cheering cup side missing final

indicators.note: missing its final letter, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a team is a side in sport

explanation.surface: A team losing a cup final, needing cheering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup final' looks like a match; 'cup' belongs to the definition, the cup that cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is often called the cup that cheers, a reviving drink.

clue.text: Strange of Irish to keep potential worker in isolation

indicators.note: the outer word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: quare is Irish dialect for strange
an ant may be a worker ant

explanation.surface: An odd Irish arrangement keeps a would-be employee apart from others.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is enforced separation to stop disease spreading, a form of isolation.

clue.text: Fought to be heard in support of a grant

indicators.note: in a down answer the next piece sits below, supporting the first
to be heard means spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: warred means fought

explanation.surface: Soldiers fought, it is said, to back a funding bid.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum given or granted, as in a student award.

clue.text: Minister: a politician getting makeover

parts.note: a minister of religion is a Reverend, abbreviated Rev
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A government minister and an MP are given an image overhaul.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp something is to renovate or give it a new look, a makeover.

clue.text: Old priest's last letter discovered in time

indicators.note: found inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An ancient cleric's final letter turns up within a historical period.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra was a Jewish priest and scribe of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Awfully mean, not embracing players leaving

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the next piece in their arms
awfully indicates the letters are badly arranged

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Mean and stingy, refusing to hug the departing actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' looks like actors in the scene, but here they are musicians; 'leaving' is a noun, the act of departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandonment is the act of deserting or quitting something.

clue.text: Exercise system of irrational evening shifts?

parts.note: pi is the famous irrational number
lates are late shifts at work

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a workout regime has silly late hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a method of exercise focusing on core strength and posture.

clue.text: Load on vessel includes scraps ultimately given to crow

indicators.note: the larger word takes in the letter given

parts.note: a boatful is the load a boat carries

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

explanation.surface: A boat's cargo of leftovers is thrown to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird; here it is the verb, to brag.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag, so someone given to it is inclined to boast.

clue.text: An idea, alas, or odd composition that's very much late!

indicators.note: a composition puts the given letters together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone muses that an odd idea or composition is something long since gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the five words AN IDEA ALAS OR ODD; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean deceased; the idiom describes something utterly and certainly dead.

clue.text: Weird blooming network with satellite receiver

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out
LAN, local area network
a dish aerial receives satellite signals

explanation.surface: A strange flowering computer network fitted with a satellite dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish means bizarre or strikingly unfamiliar, i.e. strange.

clue.text: Explosive, overwhelming greeting offends volunteers right now

indicators.note: the explosive swamps the rest, surrounding them

parts.note: TNT, trinitrotoluene
hi is a greeting
to sin is to offend
TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A volatile, effusive greeting upsets volunteers immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: This instant means immediately, at once, without delay.

clue.text: Passage which Cockney has to be finished?

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: to have had it is to be done for, finished

explanation.surface: A question about which tunnel a Londoner is obliged to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London accent that drops initial H, so HAD IT becomes 'AD IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal entrance tunnel into a mine, a kind of passage.

clue.text: TV show one's watching all the time?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the reality show filming housemates
second meaning: the ever-watchful state figure of Orwell's 1984

explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to describe a viewer; Orwell's line 'Big Brother is watching you' supplies the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the reality television programme and the surveillance leader in Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Windcheater?

parts.note: read as wind plus cheater: a whirlwind and also a swindler

explanation.walkthrough: A windcheater looks like a jacket, but split it: the answer is both a whirling wind and a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a tornado and also a dishonest person who swindles others.

clue.text: Beer right after wine, when one's ready for anything?

indicators.note: the beer comes after the wine in order

parts.note: red is red wine
ale is beer
RT, abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Beer straight after wine, at the point when a drinker will take on anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is the highest state of readiness for an emergency.

clue.text: Sat thus starting off sitcom?

indicators.note: says the day named begins in the way the answer describes, when the day before is over

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday, the day after Friday

explanation.surface: Someone sat down this way to begin watching a TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sat' as Saturday: it begins when Fri ends, giving the US sitcom's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends is the long-running American television situation comedy.

clue.text: Maybe went down the pub, then dropped round

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: to shed is to drop, as leaves are shed
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone popped down the pub and then went round dropping in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went down the pub' looks like a single phrase; the definition stops at 'went down', as one shins down a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To shin is to climb using arms and legs, up or down, so descending a pole is an example.

clue.text: A few supposed greeting to be for an unknown reason

parts.note: some means a few
'How!' is the greeting given to Native Americans in old Westerns, hence supposed

explanation.surface: Some purported greeting with no obvious explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: Somehow can mean for some reason that is not clear or not known.

clue.text: Woefully misled British politicians

indicators.note: woefully suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lament that British politicians have been sadly misled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lib Dems (Liberal Democrats) are a UK political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Lib Dems are members of the Liberal Democrat party, so they are politicians.

clue.text: Shout I didn't hear that's upset poet

indicators.note: in a down answer upset turns the pieces upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: to yell is to shout
'eh?' asks for repetition
the 's of that's stands for is, giving S

explanation.surface: A shout that went unheard upsets a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Widespread celebration?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on a large scale
second meaning: the Eucharist, celebrated in church

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a nationwide party; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means large-scale; the noun is the Catholic service where the priest celebrates the Eucharist.

clue.text: Copper receptacle put with waste

parts.note: to blue money is to squander it, a British usage
a bottle is a container

explanation.surface: A copper container placed with the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal of the receptacle; it is slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is old British slang for a policeman, from the blue uniform.

clue.text: Graceful runner with energy — and light

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to light on is to land or alight

explanation.surface: An elegant athlete runs with vigour and a light step.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, a running animal of grace.

clue.text: What might have wings for doing bird flap

definitions.text: What might have wings for doing bird
definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for prison, where one does bird (serves time) and which has wings

explanation.walkthrough: Wings and bird suggest a flying creature; doing bird is British slang for serving a jail sentence, and prisons have wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for jail, and a stir is also a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Great disappointment, where you'd stay single

parts.note: heartbreak is overwhelming sorrow or disappointment
a hotel is where you stay when away

explanation.surface: A big letdown about where a lone traveller would lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like a single room; it is a record, the 1956 Elvis Presley hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak Hotel was Elvis Presley's first big hit record released as a single.

clue.text: That's the case model has to lift

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting the word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Fashion modelling requires one to lift a case.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Tis is the poetic contraction of it is, affirming something is true.

clue.text: Finish off expression in method that's far from neat

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the next one

parts.note: a way is a method

indicators.note: to finish off a word here is to remove its last letter

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: Advice on how to end a remark that is untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is the drinker's word for undiluted, so a watery drink is far from neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink served neat has no water added; a diluted one is the opposite.

clue.text: Article in papers concerning for one potentially

indicators.note: the article is put inside papers plus concerning, joined

parts.note: ID, identity papers
re means about or concerning
a is the indefinite article
say is used for 'for example'

explanation.surface: An item placed in newspapers about one possible case.
explanation.definitionFit: I dare say expresses that something is likely or possible, much as perhaps does.
